clue.text: Writer's employed reworking fictional detective

indicators.note: reworking says the letters of the preceding words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An author's hired help is busy redrafting a story about a made-up sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworking' rearranges the fifteen letters of WRITERS EMPLOYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers's aristocratic amateur sleuth is a famous detective of crime fiction.

clue.text: Clean up American city falling short

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
falling short means coming in under the mark

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy a US city that is not meeting its targets.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash clothes, or to clean up dirty money by passing it through legitimate channels.

clue.text: English change course overturning old magistrate

indicators.note: in a down clue overturning turns the letters of the pieces upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: to veer is to change course

explanation.surface: An English official is overruled when a court reverses its direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval local official or magistrate, as in shire-reeve, the origin of sheriff.

clue.text: Leader needs trip abroad

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered or astray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A head of state requires a foreign visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is a head of state or the chief of an organisation.

clue.text: Irritable if brought in to give evidence

indicators.note: brought in says the word if is placed within the synonym for irritable

parts.note: testy means irritable

explanation.surface: A tetchy witness is called into court to give testimony.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to make a statement under oath as a witness.

clue.text: Upper-class punished again?

definitions.meaning: cultivated and elegant, like the upper class
the question mark flags the pun

explanation.surface: A posh person penalised a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished, genteel manners are associated with the upper class; a second penalty would be a re-fining.

clue.text: Birdbrain's regularly forgotten first name of actor

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is dropped in turn, leaving the second, fourth, sixth and so on

explanation.surface: A scatterbrain keeps failing to remember a star's forename.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping B, R, B, A, N from BIRDBRAINS leaves the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris Elba is a well-known British actor, so this is his given name.

clue.text: Something cold in reptile devouring variety of fowl

indicators.note: devouring means the reptile swallows the rearranged bird letters into its middle

parts.note: a snake is a reptile

indicators.note: a variety of the word means its letters in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded snake swallows a chicken of some breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' in the surface goes with cold-blooded reptiles, but the definition wants a frozen object; 'variety of' reorders the bird before 'devouring' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A single crystal of falling ice is a cold thing indeed.

clue.text: Dairy products turn up in nomads' dwellings

indicators.note: in places the reversed turn inside the tents

parts.note: yurts are the round felt tents of Central Asian nomads

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Milk products show up in the tents of wandering herders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG, placed 'in' YURTS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fermented milk foods, so they count among dairy goods.

clue.text: It's futile to economise, apparently

definitions.meaning: futile means pointless, having no effect

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that saving money is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointless serves no purpose; read as two words it describes cutting consumption.

clue.text: Sprinters used to run this and roll up on finishing at last

parts.note: to furl is to roll up, as a sail or flag

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word finishing

explanation.surface: Athletes once raced a set distance and wound up the tape at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sprint races were run over an eighth of a mile, a racing distance of 220 yards.

clue.text: Adviser on board initiated changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company director starts making reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a company board, but here it means food, as in bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition professional advises on what you eat, and board is an old word for meals.

clue.text: Match official since turning round taking fewer chances

indicators.note: turning round says the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: REF is short for referee
as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'

explanation.surface: A referee playing it cautious, having turned to face the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking fewer risks makes one more secure, the comparative of secure from danger.

clue.text: It's a crime — ecstasy smuggled by Welsh comedian, not mafia boss

indicators.note: smuggled by says the drug is slipped inside what is left of the comedian
not removes the boss's title from the comedian's name

parts.note: Rob Brydon is a Welsh comedian and actor
a Don is a Mafia chief
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Welsh comic caught trafficking drugs, though not on a mob boss's orders, is committing an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob Brydon is a Welsh comedian known from Gavin and Stacey; 'not' drops the boss, leaving ROBBRY, and 'smuggled by' slips the drug inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking property by force or theft is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Encapsulated by symbol of Christ rising, a little part is related to religious ceremony

indicators.note: encapsulated by says the following pieces sit inside the reversed symbol
in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Lamb of God is a symbol of Christ
PT is a short form of part

explanation.surface: A sacred emblem frames a small detail that is linked to a church rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the Lamb of God upwards to BMAL, and 'Encapsulated by' wraps it round the little part.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening is a church rite, and the adjective describes things connected with it, such as a font.

clue.text: Pounds secured by cheat with Scandinavian money

indicators.note: secured by places the pound sign after the cheat, held by it

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra
Lars is a common Scandinavian man's name

explanation.surface: British currency swindled and swapped for a Nordic man's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The US currency unit in the plural is simply cash or money.

clue.text: I hail aunt touring European country

indicators.note: touring suggests letters wandering about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller greets a relative on holiday in a Baltic nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic state, it is a nation of Europe.

clue.text: Laurel given to international player — it might result in a wind-up

definitions.text: it might result in a wind-up

indicators.note: given to says Laurel's name is attached after the player

parts.note: a cap is a player chosen for a national side
Stan Laurel was the thin half of Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A sporting honour awarded to a national team member could cause annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' looks like a victor's wreath but is the comedian. A wind-up is also British slang for a tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's revolving drum hauls in cable by winding it round.

clue.text: Geordie perhaps captivated by brash Londoner

indicators.note: captivated by says the regional letters are held inside the word for brash

parts.note: cocky means brash and over-confident
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East, NE

explanation.surface: A Newcastle native charmed by a loud-mouthed man from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a person from Tyneside in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional East End Londoner, born within the sound of Bow bells.

clue.text: Watch people on the up eclipsing second greatest rivals

indicators.note: eclipsing means covering, so the reversed pair surrounds the letter for second
in a down clue on the up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to see is to watch
men means people

explanation.surface: Stargazers witness an eclipse while racing their closest competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' reverses SEEMEN to NEMEES; 'eclipsing' holds S within.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch-enemies, from Nemesis the Greek goddess of retribution.

clue.text: Begin to pick different second-class ingredient

indicators.note: begin to picks the opening letter of pick

parts.note: other means different
B is the grade below A, second class

explanation.surface: Instructions to start choosing an alternative cheaper component.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy plant used for cooking, a vegetable or herb for the pot, is a component of dishes.

clue.text: Lacking motor, passengers might take this

definitions.text: Lacking motor, passengers might take this

parts.words: Lacking motor, passengers might take this
parts.note: a vehicle powered by pedal rather than engine that carries fares, like a taxi

explanation.surface: Without a car, travellers could hop on one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle rickshaw carries passengers by pedal power, with no engine.

clue.text: Some wombles smell? That's surprising

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking whether the Wombles, litter-collecting creatures of British children's TV, give off an odour.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation of astonishment, like goodness me.

clue.text: It's rather cold with central heating not right

parts.note: ill means not right, unwell

explanation.surface: A room is cool because the heating has broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Chill as an adjective means unpleasantly cool, somewhat cold.

clue.text: Keep still in boat as attempt to deceive

definitions.meaning: a nautical phrase for a ship stopping, heading to wind with little way on

explanation.surface: Sitting motionless on a vessel as a ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing term for halting a vessel, and also telling someone untruths.

clue.text: Played minor part in what fraudulent statistician did?

definitions.meaning: filled a place merely to complete a team or group
a cheating statistician would invent figures; the question mark flags the literal reading

explanation.surface: A dishonest data analyst only had a bit role.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being present only to fill a quota, read literally as faking the figures.

clue.text: Rates got by casual worker on start of internship

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of internship

explanation.surface: A temporary employee's pay rates at the beginning of a placement.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical speeds are called these, the plural of the Italian term for pace.

clue.text: See 23
Broadcast of wrongdoer spoils entertainment venues

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a wrongdoer is a sinner, and spoils means mars

explanation.surface: Transmitting a criminal's escapades ruins the evening's entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNER MARS said quickly gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture houses where films are shown are places of entertainment.

clue.text: Chicken roll featured in song from the 1960s

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, chicken
a submarine is a long bread roll filled as a sandwich

explanation.surface: A chicken sandwich appeared in a sixties hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1966 Beatles hit, so it is a song of that decade.
